name: Selection float menu (shared FloatMenu: Note / Dialogue / Search / Deep-research)

name: Reader typography, measure and prose layer (BookReader / ReadingColumn)
gap: Main has no rich document model and the column does not own its measure. It stays short of the 60–72ch Kindle bar until W3 merges. Rich blocks (lists, tables, math) need the stranded Reader.tsx or new work.

name: Page-turn keys (arrows / space / PageDown)
gap: ←/→, space, PageUp/PageDown and Home/End need wiring to setPageIndex, with focus-scope rules so the keys never fire inside inputs or FloatMenu.

name: Progress indicator
gap: There is no progress bar, no percentage, no chapter-remaining count, no time-left estimate, and no progress shown on library or home cards.

name: Reading position persistence and cross-device sync
gap: No durable or cross-device position (the D5 bar). Position is also clobbered when a book is opened from a citation.

name: Distraction-free / focus mode
gap: No prefix+f mode that hides chrome down to the path header.

name: Day/night reading themes
gap: No per-reader night toggle and no sepia or paper theme. Dark mode has known contrast defects (the reader error text measures 3.25:1).

name: Text size / font controls
gap: No reader Aa control (size, line height, margins, font). Pagination does not depend on text size (usePosition.ts docblock), so adding size controls will not break saved positions.

name: Layout stability while loading
gap: Even with W3 the skeleton is not shaped like the final TOC and column. Scroll reset on page turn was NOT MEASURED.

name: PDF reading (PdfViewer / Wrestle)
gap: PDFs are not a readable book surface: one page only, no page links and no annotation layer.

name: Footnote / endnote parsing and rendering
gap: Footnotes are either deleted at ingest or left as dead text. A #fn anchor on a different page window cannot resolve, because paginate() splits the body into per-page DOMs (paginate.ts:23-60).

name: Click behaviour for links inside the reader body
gap: D5 requires 'never a navigation away'. Nothing turns a link click into a child tab or window.

name: In-product citation to source opening
gap: No single openDocument resolver. Citations either navigate away or open a flat window, and none records parentage.

name: Resolving a reference (DOI / arXiv id) to a library document, or ingesting it on demand
gap: There is no reader-facing 'resolve this reference' call (look up by DOI or arXiv id in the graph, else offer rights-aware ingest). There is also no reference-list extraction for papers.

name: Opening a document from a document (workspace windows)
gap: The windows are flat and floating, capped at 8, and not persisted. They cannot represent an unbounded rabbit hole, and there is no lineage to return along.

name: Research spun from a passage, with lineage and return
gap: The research branch does not open as a child tab next to the passage. The way back relies on sessionStorage position, and the branch record is not a typed origin {doc_id, locator}.

name: Reusable tree structures (unbounded depth)
gap: These trees cover investigations, chats and TOCs, not tabs. The D6 visual rules (indent capped at 6 levels plus a depth badge, hierarchical numbers, focus-subtree) are not implemented anywhere.

name: Branch-tab tree (D6) and any tab concept in the reader
gap: The whole D6 surface is unbuilt: tab model, path header, sibling strip, tree panel, numbers as addresses, prune/lift with undo, and persistence.

name: Tree navigation keys (parent / child / sibling / tree panel)
gap: The prefix+u/o/n/p/t keys and their direct-chord twins (D2/D6) are missing, and browser-reserved combos (bindings.ts:438-462) limit the choices.

name: Breadcrumb path / back to passage
gap: No root-to-current path of documents, and no 'return to the exact passage' beyond the sessionStorage page index.

name: Saved reads (/readings PersonalSpace)
gap: This list is 'what I have read', not a to-read queue or a continue shelf. It could feed Continue once a position exists.

name: User read flags / read later / bookmarks
gap: No flag entity on documents or passages. THREAD-CONTRACT §2.8 proposes a single flag entity with intent read|diligence and actor user|agent, unsigned.

name: Agent-suggested reading / an agent flagging something to read
gap: No agent can put an item in a to-read queue with who, why and which project (the D5 'To read' door).

name: Prompt-to-curate shelf
gap: Curation lasts only for the session. It is not saved as a queue and not tied to a project.

name: Reading home: three doors (continue / to read / new)
gap: Only the 'New' door exists (library, search, import). Continue and To-read are missing, and a standalone book has no reading workstation (Q-A5).

name: Continue reading
gap: Needs a server-side position per (owner, document), joined with source.read history.
